facts.t: Article 21 is the shortest article that does the most work
facts.d: It runs to a single sentence. From it the Supreme Court has read the rights to livelihood, shelter, food, water, education, health, privacy, sleep, a clean environment, and to die with dignity — an expansion with almost no parallel in comparative constitutional law.

facts.t: Kharak Singh contained the dissent that won 55 years later
facts.d: The 1962 majority refused to recognise privacy as a right. Justice Subba Rao's dissent said the opposite. Puttaswamy (2017) — nine judges, unanimous — vindicated the dissent and overruled the majority.

facts.t: India has no explicit constitutional right to a clean environment
facts.d: Articles 48A and 51A(g), added by the 42nd Amendment, are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty — neither directly enforceable. Every environmental claim must therefore be anchored to Article 21, which makes enforcement contingent and reactive.

bank.q: With reference to Maneka Gandhi (1978), consider the following statements:
s: It converted procedure established by law into a test of due process.
Where a matter concerns both Articles 19 and 21, all of Articles 14, 19 and 21 must be satisfied.
It overruled Gian Kaur on the right to die.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Gian Kaur was decided in 1996, eighteen years later, and could not have been overruled by Maneka Gandhi.

bank.q: The right to privacy was recognised as a fundamental right, with a proportionality test, in:
bank.e: Puttaswamy (2017) located privacy in Articles 21 and 19 and overruled the contrary holdings in M. P. Sharma and Kharak Singh.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (right read into Article 21):
pairs: 3. Right against the adverse effects of climate change
bank.e: Olga Tellis gave livelihood, Chameli Singh shelter, PUCL food, and Ranjitsinh a distinct right against the adverse effects of climate change, grounded in Articles 21 and 14.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about euthanasia in India?
o: Passive euthanasia is legal subject to safeguards
Active euthanasia attracts liability under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
Gian Kaur held that Article 21 includes the right to die
Common Cause (2018) validated advance medical directives
bank.e: Gian Kaur held that Article 21 does not include a right to die — but it distinguished euthanasia from suicide, which is what opened the door to Aruna Shanbaug and Common Cause.

bank.as: India still has no standalone euthanasia statute.
bank.rs: End-of-life decisions are governed by Supreme Court guidelines rather than by legislation.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The 2023 review simplified the Common Cause procedure, and Harish Rana (2026) expressly urged Parliament to legislate.

bank.q: With reference to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, consider the following:
s: It applies only to digital personal data and has extraterritorial reach.
It adopts a negative-list approach to cross-border transfers.
Appeals from the Data Protection Board lie to the High Court.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Appeals lie to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal, not to the High Court.

bank.q: Under the DPDP Act, a personal data breach must be reported in a detailed report within:
bank.e: Intimation must be without delay and the detailed report within 72 hours — mirroring the GDPR timeline.

bank.q: All of the following are criticisms of the DPDP Act EXCEPT:
o: Wide state exemptions under section 17 without independent oversight
The amendment to section 8(1)(j) removing the RTI public-interest balancing test
Turnover-linked penalties that are disproportionate to Indian business realities
Board members appointed and conditioned by the Centre, risking executive capture
bank.e: India's penalties are capped in absolute rupee terms, up to ₹250 crore — not turnover-linked. Turnover-linked fines of 4% are the GDPR model, cited as a lesson India might learn from.

bank.q: Arrange the following environmental milestones in correct chronological order:
items: Vellore Citizens' Forum introduces the precautionary principle
RLEK recognises a right to a healthy environment
M. C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath applies the public trust doctrine
M. C. Mehta establishes a pollution-free environment as a fundamental right
bank.e: RLEK (1985) → M. C. Mehta (1986) → Vellore Citizens' Forum (1996) → M. C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997).

bank.q: The doctrine of absolute liability, which admits no exceptions, emerged from:
bank.e: The Oleum gas leak case produced absolute liability, deliberately stricter than the English rule in Rylands v. Fletcher, which allows defences.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the golden triangle:
s: Article 14 supplies reasonable classification and anti-arbitrariness.
Article 21 now imports principles of natural justice.
Where only Article 21 is engaged, Article 19 must still be independently satisfied.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Where only Article 21 is engaged, Articles 14 and 21 must be satisfied — Article 19 comes in only when the matter also concerns one of its freedoms.

bank.as: Harish Rana (2026) is described as the first order actually implementing passive euthanasia.
bank.rs: The Court held that clinically assisted nutrition and hydration counts as medical treatment that may be withdrawn.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — classifying CANH as treatment is exactly what made withdrawal legally possible, and the 30-day cooling-off period was waived.
